title: Access provisioning & SSO onboarding — Sable Therapeutics
transcript:
Meeting header: 
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 14:30 PT (21:30Z)
Recorded duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Artifacts referenced: SSO checklist deck (link: https://redwood.example/sso-checklist), customer security questionnaire (sable-drive/SEC-Q-2025.pdf)

Summary (auto): Sable Therapeutics is evaluating Redwood for hosted inference with strict least-privileged access requirements. Main topics: SAML/SSO configuration, SCIM provisioning cadence, RBAC model and default roles, audit log retention and event export, KMS integration and envelope encryption, SOC2 evidence requests and data residency concerns. Action: Redwood to share SAML metadata and sample SCIM payloads; Sable to provide internal RBAC matrix and preferred KMS provider.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): All right hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can folks hear me?
[00:04] Janelle (Sable): Yep, loud and clear.
[00:06] Marcus (Sable): Good here.
[00:08] Owen (Redwood SE): Great — Im Owen, security engineer on the account, Ill run through the provisioning and RBAC pieces with you.
[00:15] Janelle: Cool, our primary goals today are SSO onboarding and making sure we can map least-privilege roles to our org around PHI handling. Weve got a SOC 2 in progress and want to close gaps.
[00:22] Owen: Understood. Quick agenda: SAML metadata & IdP flows, SCIM sync frequency and SCIM attribute mapping, RBAC roles and custom scopes, audit logs / export for evidentiary purposes, KMS / encryption at rest, and then Q&A.
[00:33] Devon (Sable): Wanted to flag we use Okta as IdP and AWS KMS (custom CMK) for critical keys.
[00:38] Maya: Perfect, thats aligned to what weve seen. We support Okta SAML, and we have a private-key integration with customer-managed KMS for private deployments and Dedicated, and for hosted we do a managed KMS but can also integrate via external key wrap.
[00:48] Marcus: When you say "integrate" — is that via an envelope key? I want to understand key ownership and whether the key material ever leaves our HSM.
[00:56] Owen: Yes, we use envelope encryption. For Private deployments you can provision a CMK and we call out to KMS for key unwrap — Redwood never stores plaintext root keys. For Hosted we can do BYOK via AWS KMS external key wrap or a partner HSM — theres a short latency cost but thats the recommended pattern.
[01:12] Marcus: Okay, good. Also, audit log retention — our compliance team needs event-level logs for a minimum of 2 years for select actions. How granular are your logs?
[01:20] Owen: We track audit events per-token for control plane actions (model deploy, config change, API key lifecycle) and per-request headers for user-level request metadata. Logs can be exported to your S3 or forwarded to Splunk/Datadog; retention is configurable on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we provide 90-day retention by default, with add-ons for longer retention.
[01:37] Janelle: So for Hosted we'd need an enterprise add-on to meet 2 years?
[01:40] Maya: Correct, that's part of the compliance package. We'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[01:45] [00:45] Devon: On SCIM — we want automated deprovisioning, can the SCIM events be real-time or are they batched?
[00:51] Owen: SCIM is offered as near-real-time push from your IdP. Typical cadence is immediate on changes; we also support periodic full-syncs nightly for reconciliation. The SCIM schema supports groups and entitlements mapping so you can map AD groups to Redwood roles.
[01:05] Marcus: Any constraints on attribute mapping? We have custom attributes for 'data-classification:phi' and similar.
[01:10] Owen: We support custom attributes in SCIM upserts, well share a sample payload. Caveat: role enforcement is via RBAC layer which consumes the SCIM group-to-role mapping; custom attributes can be used for logging and tagging but not currently for dynamic policy evaluation (we can roadmap attribute-based access control if you need).
[01:27] Janelle: That's fine for now, as long as we can tag and later filter audit events by those attributes.
[01:31] Owen: Yep, you can add tags to requests and those propagate to logs.
[01:35] [01:35] Maya: Let's walk through a typical SSO setup — Owen, can you summarize?
[01:38] Owen: Sure. Steps: 1) Redwood provides SAML metadata (SP metadata) — that's the file you'll upload into Okta. 2) Okta returns IdP metadata and SAML cert; we exchange the entity IDs and endpoints. 3) We enable SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows and test with a small pilot group. 4) SCIM provisioning hook is configured in Okta to post to our SCIM endpoint with the shared bearer token.
[01:57] Marcus: For the SCIM bearer token, can we rotate it regularly and do you support JWK-based auth?
[02:03] Owen: We currently support rotating bearer tokens and short-lived tokens via the console. JWK-based client auth is on the roadmap — not GA yet.
[02:10] Devon: If a token is compromised, whats the blast radius?
[02:13] Owen: SCIM tokens are scoped only to provisioning APIs; they dont grant inference API access. We also recommend IP allow-listing and SCIM webhooks behind your VPN for extra protection.
[02:24] Janelle: Walk me through the RBAC roles you expose out of the box.
[02:27] Owen: Default roles: Admin (full control), Developer (deploy models, view logs), Auditor (read-only for logs and configs), Viewer (read access to usage and run outputs), and Operator (manage capacity/budgeting). You can create custom roles with a fine-grained permission matrix — create, read, update, delete per resource.
[02:44] Marcus: We need a least-privilege policy where only a handful of admins can deploy models that access PHI, while dev teams can run inference on synthetic/test data. Is there a way to bind roles to model tags or to environment?
[02:54] Owen: Yes, role bindings can be scoped to projects and model tags; you can create policy like "deploy:models" only if tag != 'prod-phi' or only in a sandbox namespace. The console UI and API expose those constraints.
[03:07] Devon: Great. On the evidence front for SOC 2, will you provide exported logs and a mapping document for control implementation?
[03:13] Maya: We provide SOC 2 artifact bundle for enterprise — policy docs, logs export samples, pen test results, and a control-matrix matching to common frameworks. For Hosted customers we have a scoping questionnaire to provide you with the correct artifacts.
[03:25] Marcus: Do you have a maintained AICPA SOC 2 report we can request?
[03:28] Maya: Yes, we have a SOC 2 Type II report; we'll arrange an NDA flow if you need the full report.
[03:34] [03:34] Janelle: About data residency — some of our PHI must stay in us-east-1 region and within US boundaries. How do you guarantee region pinning for hosted?
[03:42] Owen: For Hosted we provide region pinning at account level — requests are routed only to chosen region endpoints. For higher assurance we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated in a VPC in your region or Private deployment.
[03:54] Marcus: Any limitations on latency or data egress when pinning?
[03:57] Owen: Minimal — the main tradeoff is capacity availability during peak; our routing policies will attempt local capacity then fall back within your consented regions only.
[04:05] Devon: On RBAC audit — can role changes and grant events be forwarded to our SIEM as they happen?
[04:10] Owen: Yes, we emit admin events; these can be streamed to your logging endpoint in near real-time. We also persist the event detail in the audit store for retrieval.
[04:18] [04:18] Maya: A few gotchas we typically see: 1) SCIM group names mismatch — ensure your group-to-role mapping is agreed up front. 2) Clock skew in SAML assertions — synchronize NTP across IdP/SP. 3) For BYOK there is an integration test to validate key policies and IAM roles.
[04:36] Janelle: For the SCIM pilot, who should be the first users we onboard?
[04:39] Maya: Start with a single team (two admins, three power-users) and a sandbox project. That allows us to validate mappings and deprovisioning behavior.
[04:46] Marcus: We also wanted to discuss log formats — CSV vs JSON, can you do structured JSON with fields we can parse?
[04:52] Owen: All event exports are structured JSON with typed fields (timestamp, actor, action, resource, attrs). We can provide schema and example logs.
[04:59] Devon: One small thing — in your docs you mention "KV cache" for inference caching; sometimes our compliance folks misread it. Can you include a short note on what cached data is stored and retention?
[05:08] Owen: Sure. We cache model key-value state (not request payloads) to speed up inference; request-level prefix caching is optional and can be disabled. We can add note that cached state doesn't include customer prompt persistence unless you opt-in for longer contexts.
[05:22] [05:22] Janelle: Anything else on encryption-in-transit?
[05:25] Owen: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, we support mutual TLS for Private deployments and mTLS for dedicated endpoints.
[05:31] Maya: Okay, lets go through remaining Qs from your security questionnaire — Marcus had a list?
[05:36] Marcus: Yes, quick callouts: 1) Do you rotate service account credentials automatically? 2) How are secrets used by workers stored? 3) Is there a dedicated pen-test cadence?
[05:45] Owen: 1) We provide rotation for service keys and recommend short-lived tokens with our SDK. 2) Secrets used by workers are in a per-environment secret store (encrypted with KMS) with RBAC. 3) Pen tests annually and after major infra changes; reports available under NDA.
[05:57] Janelle: Great.
[05:59] Maya: Quick recap of asked deliverables and next steps.
[06:02] Maya: Owen will send the SP metadata plus a sample SCIM payload and attribute mapping.
[06:06] Owen: Ill include a sample SCIM patch and a JSON body with custom attribute examples and group to role map.
[06:11] Maya: I will also include the SOC 2 sharing instructions and compliance add-on pricing.
[06:15] Devon: Well send our RBAC matrix and indicate which groups contain PHI access.
[06:19] Marcus: We'll also confirm our KMS key ARN and desired retention for logs.
[06:22] Maya: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:24] Janelle: No, thats it from us — thanks.
[06:26] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[06:28] (call ends)

Notes: Transcription had a few mis-typed terms ("KVM" instead of KMS in auto captions; "prefix cache" occasionally transcribed as "press cache"). Action items below consolidated.
